args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 deploy (error rate 18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west, eu-west). Attempted rollback to v2.3.0 (most recent healthy prod release) was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined (CVE-2026-4417). Rolled back checkout-api to v2.2.9 (the next most recent release that was healthy in production) in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west); rollout completed and verified. Follow-ups: investigate root cause of v2.3.1 failure; note that the service is now two releases behind and v2.3.0 remains unavailable due to the CVE quarantine.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

**Diagnosis**
- checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy and staging-only, so not a candidate).

**Rollback**
- Attempted rollback to v2.3.0 → **rejected**: v2.3.0 is quarantined under CVE-2026-4417.
- Rolled back to **v2.2.9** instead (the next most recent release that was healthy in production). Rollout completed in all three regions.
- Post-rollback status: **healthy**, error rate 0.2%, v2.2.9 everywhere.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api; on-call has been paged. The summary documents the failure, the quarantined v2.3.0 attempt, the v2.2.9 rollback, and follow-ups (root-cause v2.3.1; note the service is now two releases behind with v2.3.0 unavailable due to the CVE).

One thing worth flagging to the team: since v2.3.0 is blocked by the CVE, the forward-fix path will need to be a patched build on top of v2.3.1 rather than a return to v2.3.0.
